facility: Williams Geismar Olefins Plant, propylene fractionator reboiler rupture and fire, Geismar, Louisiana, June 13, 2013
source: U.S. Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board, Williams Geismar Olefins Plant Reboiler Rupture and Fire, Case Study No. 2013-03-I-LA, October 2016 (public record)
question: On June 13, 2013, propylene fractionator Reboiler B at the Williams Geismar olefins plant ruptured about three minutes after an operations supervisor opened the hot quench water (about 187 F) to its tubes; it had been offline on standby for 16 months since maintenance in February 2012, when it was reportedly left filled with nitrogen behind single closed block valves on its shell-side inlet and outlet. Shell side process fluid: about 95% propane, balance mostly propylene and C4s. Reboiler B shell design: maximum allowable working pressure 300 psig, hydrostatic test 450 psig. Using the facility description, the schematic and the incident timeline, determine the failure mechanism and estimate with calculations the pressures that could be reached in the shell, explain why the reboiler was not protected from overpressure, and recommend the design, procedural and management changes that would prevent a recurrence.

criteria.name: C-01 Overpressure protection path must remain open
criteria.source: p.9: 'If the new valves were not in the proper position (open or closed) for each phase of operation, the reboiler could be isolated from its protective pressure relief valve located on top of the propylene fractionator (Figure 4).' + p.10 Fig.4 legend 'Pressure relief valve protected propylene fractionator and shells of Reboilers A and B'
criteria.value: Reboiler A/B shells protected only via fractionator overhead PRV; 2001 shell-side gate valves can isolate shell from PRV = hazard

criteria.name: C-02 Operating philosophy - single-reboiler continuous operation
criteria.source: p.9: 'In 2001, Williams installed valves on the shell-side and tube-side reboiler piping to allow for continuous operation with only one reboiler operating at a time. The other reboiler would be offline but ready for operation (see Section 5.1), isolated from the process by the new valves.'
criteria.value: One reboiler in service, one offline isolated standby; firm capacity = one reboiler with largest (other) unit out of service

criteria.name: C-03 Tube-side heating medium temperature
criteria.source: p.9: 'Quench water enters the propylene fractionator reboilers at approximately 185 degF'
criteria.value: approx 185 F quench water inlet (task brief states about 187 F - see RFI-02)

criteria.name: C-04 Shell-side process fluid composition and inlet temperature
criteria.source: p.9: 'tube-side hot quench water vaporizes shell-side hydrocarbon process fluid, which is approximately 95% propane with the balance composed mostly of propylene and C4s' + 'which enters the reboiler at a temperature of approximately 130 degF'
criteria.value: approx 95% propane, balance propylene + C4s; shell inlet approx 130 F

criteria.name: C-05 Standby duration before failure
criteria.source: p.6: 'Reboiler B had been offline for 16 months while Reboiler A was in operation' + p.11 incident date June 13, 2013
criteria.value: 16 months offline (Feb 2012 to June 2013 per task brief - to be verified RFI-04)

criteria.name: C-06 Failure timeline
criteria.source: p.11: 'at 8:33 am, the operations supervisor likely opened the quench water valves on the offline reboiler, Reboiler B' + 'Approximately three minutes later, Reboiler B exploded.' + p.12 Fig.6 caption 'Reboiler B ruptures approximately three minutes later.'
criteria.value: Hot water admission ~08:33, rupture ~3 min later

criteria.name: C-07 Shell mechanical limits - UNVERIFIED, from task brief
criteria.source: Task brief (not in p.6-13): shell MAWP 300 psig, hydrostatic test 450 psig - See RFI-03 for verification
criteria.value: ASSUMPTION for scoping only: MAWP 300 psig, hydrotest 450 psig. Reason: provided in task brief; no page citation in 6-13; must verify from nameplate/dossier before any pressure calculation

criteria.name: C-08 Fouling service duty
criteria.source: p.8: 'some oily material remains in the quench water. Over time, some of this material adheres to and builds up on the inside of process equipment such as heat exchanger tubes, resulting in a decrease in both heat transfer efficiency and quench water flow rate. The buildup of such material is called fouling.' + p.6 fn7
criteria.value: Quench-water-side fouling reduces flow and heat transfer; triggers nonroutine switching activity

criteria.name: C-09 Consequence severity baseline
criteria.source: p.11: 'launched a portion of the propylene fractionator reboiler piping into a pipe rack approximately 30 feet overhead' + p.12: 'fire lasted approximately 3.5 hours, and Williams reported releasing over 30,000 pounds of flammable hydrocarbons'
criteria.value: 30 ft missile throw, 3.5 h fire, >30,000 lb release - confirms catastrophic shell rupture, not tube leak

In 2001, Williams installed valves on the shell-side and tube-side reboiler piping to allow for continuous operation with only one reboiler operating at a time.

If the new valves were not in the proper position (open or closed) for each phase of operation, the reboiler could be isolated from its protective pressure relief valve located on top of the propylene fractionator (Figure 4).
The heat exchangers are 24 feet 8 inches long end-to-end.
Each exchanger shell (the portion of the heat exchanger that holds the tube bundle) is approximately 18.5 feet long and over 5 feet in diameter.
The tubes are each 3/4-inch in diameter, and each heat exchanger contains 3,020 tubes.
if one were to lay each tube from one heat exchanger end-to-end in a straight line, the tubes would span over 10.5 miles.
Depicted in Figure 3 as a two-pass heat exchanger for purposes of simplicity, the reboilers were six-pass heat exchangers.
Gate valves installed on shell-side reboiler piping in 2001
Ball valves installed on tube-side reboiler piping in 2001
Pressure relief valve protected propylene fractionator and shells of Reboilers A and B
data_register.value: one PRV on fractionator top claimed to protect both shells

data_register.quote: quench water flow through the operating propylene fractionator reboiler (Reboiler A) had dropped gradually over the past day (Figure 5).
at 8:33 am, the operations supervisor likely opened the quench water valves on the offline reboiler, Reboiler B, as indicated by the rapid increase in quench water flow rate shown in Figure 6.
Approximately three minutes later, Reboiler B exploded
launched a portion of the propylene fractionator reboiler piping into a pipe rack approximately 30 feet overhead (Figure 8).
A Williams operator working near the propylene fractionator at the time of the explosion died at the scene. The operations supervisor succumbed to severe burn injuries the next day.
167 personnel reported injuries.
Of the 167 workers who reported injuries, three were Williams employees and 164 were contractors.
The fire lasted approximately 3.5 hours
Williams reported releasing over 30,000 pounds of flammable hydrocarbons during the incident.
The plant remained down for 18 months and restarted in January 2015.

rfi.issue: RFI-01 Tag discrepancy prevents positive equipment identification
rfi.item: True tag of ruptured reboiler and P&ID lineup
rfi.reason: p.6 states EA-425B while Fig.2 p.8 labels EA-435B (and EA-435A for A). Cannot size volume or trace history without correct dossier.
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION for Steps 1-2 only: failed unit is Reboiler B (whichever tag), geometry per p.9 fn11. Reason: functional identity (B = standby 16 mo, ruptured) is consistent across pages; tag typo does not change mechanism. Verify via nameplate/P&ID before calculations.

rfi.issue: RFI-02 Hot quench water temperature conflict
rfi.item: Actual tube-side inlet temperature on June 13, 2013
rfi.reason: p.9 says approximately 185 F; task brief says about 187 F (about 187 F to tubes). 2 F matters little but historian value needed for vapor-pressure / thermal-expansion pressure estimates.
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: use 185-187 F range as upper-bound heating temperature. Reason: both sources agree hot water >>130 F shell fluid; range bounds heat input until trend retrieved. Future runs RB-HEAT-01 will use measured value.

rfi.issue: RFI-03 MAWP / hydrotest / relief setpoint not in available pages
rfi.item: Shell MAWP, hydrotest, PRV set pressure and capacity, design temperature
rfi.reason: Task brief gives MAWP 300 psig, hydrotest 450 psig, but p.6-13 contain no pressures. Cannot compare calculated trapped-liquid / boiling pressures to limits without verified limits.
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: adopt task-brief 300 psig MAWP / 450 psig hydrotest as provisional limits. Reason: provided as facility data for study; flagged UNVERIFIED. No failure-pressure conclusion to rely on them until nameplate/U-1 and PRV datasheet confirm. Future run RB-PRESS-01 will compare against verified values.

rfi.issue: RFI-04 Standby layup condition unknown from available pages
rfi.item: Feb 2012 maintenance records, nitrogen fill, which block valves closed, bleeds/drains/vents
rfi.reason: Task brief states reportedly left filled with nitrogen behind single closed block valves on shell inlet/outlet after Feb 2012; p.6 confirms 16 mo offline but gives no layup details; Sec.5.1 withheld. Determines initial inventory (nitrogen vs trapped propane liquid).
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: shell block valves were closed (isolated), tube side drained/isolated until June 13. Reason: consistent with 2001 one-reboiler philosophy (p.9) and with isolated-shell hazard (p.9-p.10). Whether liquid propane leaked in over 16 mo to be tested by drain-sample records. Future run RB-ISO-01 models both sub-cases: (a) nitrogen + leaked propane, (b) full-liquid propane.

rfi.issue: RFI-05 Trapped shell inventory composition and fill fraction
rfi.item: What and how much was inside Reboiler B shell at 08:33 (nitrogen, liquid propane/propylene/C4s, water, noncondensables)?
rfi.reason: p.9 gives operating fluid ~95% propane but not standby fluid. Pressure from heating trapped liquid to 185-187 F vs boiling/vapor-pressure vs nitrogen compression differ by orders of magnitude; fill fraction controls whether shell is hydraulically solid.
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: shell contained liquid propane mixture capable of hydraulic expansion + vaporization. Reason: 3-min rupture after hot-water admission (p.11) implies incompressible / boiling liquid present, not nitrogen gas alone which would heat slowly and vent little pressure. To be closed by sample/drain-level measurement. Future runs RB-PRESS-01 (liquid expansion) and RB-PRESS-02 (vapor pressure at 185-187 F) bound it.

rfi.issue: RFI-06 As-found valve lineup and relief-path continuity
rfi.item: Positions at 08:33-08:36 of B shell inlet gate, B shell outlet (vapor return) gate, B tube inlet/outlet ball valves, A valves, and any PRV block valves
rfi.reason: p.9-p.10 show 2001 gate valves can isolate shell from top PRV; available pages do not state actual positions. Determines whether B shell was a blocked-in volume with no relief.
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: B shell inlet and vapor-return gates were closed (blocked-in, no relief path). Reason: p.9 hazard description + fact of catastrophic rupture in ~3 min despite PRV existing on fractionator (p.10) implies no open relief path; otherwise PRV would have limited pressure. Verify via DCS/valve-stem photography and operator interviews.

rfi.issue: RFI-07 PRV adequacy and isolation details
rfi.item: PRV setpoint, relieving capacity for blocked-outlet / thermal-expansion / wetted-fire cases, inlet piping, car-seal/locked-open program for 2001 block valves
rfi.reason: Fig.4 legend claims one PRV protects fractionator + both shells, but p.9 says valves can isolate - classic API 521 violation if no dedicated thermal/expansion relief. Withheld Sec.5.1 likely covers it.
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: no dedicated shell thermal-relief and no administrative control kept relief path open. Reason: rupture occurred; if adequate thermal relief existed on isolated shell it should have prevented hydraulic burst. Recommend design change regardless; confirm via relief study and field check for thermal reliefs.

rfi.issue: RFI-08 Pre-heat pressure and temperature in B shell
rfi.item: Shell pressure/temperature just before 08:33 (ambient heating over 16 mo, solar, nitrogen pad?)
rfi.reason: No historian data in p.6-13. Initial condition anchors expansion calculation.
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: initial shell ~ ambient / ~130 F or lower, at or above propane vapor pressure if liquid present. Reason: operating inlet 130 F (p.9) is best available proxy for column sump liquid; ambient in Louisiana June also warm. Sensitivity to be run in RB-PRESS-01.

rfi.issue: RFI-09 Quantitative quench-water flows (Fig.5/Fig.6 trends without numbers)
rfi.item: Numeric flow rates through Reboiler A (fouled) and Reboiler B (newly opened) vs time
rfi.reason: p.11 references graphs but pages provide no numbers; needed to estimate heat-input rate for 3-min transient.
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: quench-water flow after opening was sufficient to heat shell inventory within minutes (evidenced by rapid flow rise per p.11-12 Fig.6 caption). Reason: qualitative trend confirms flow, not magnitude; do not assume a flow number - retrieve historian FT/FQ (see test plan TP-09). No velocity/energy computed in Steps 1-2.

rfi.issue: RFI-10 Exact shell free volume for pressure-rise estimate
rfi.item: Fabrication drawing: shell ID, bundle displacement, nozzle volumes, liquid level
rfi.reason: p.9 fn11 gives approx 18.5 ft x over 5 ft dia + 3020 x 3/4-in tubes, but over 5 ft and tube wall/displacement unknown; cannot compute trapped volume accurately.
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: use nominal 5.0-5.5 ft ID x 18.5 ft for scoping volume only; label all volumes APPROXIMATE. Reason: fn11 is approximate ('approximately', 'over'); precise calc requires U-stamp drawing. Future run RB-VOL-01 will use measured ID.

test_plan.measurements: Open/closed position of B shell inlet gate, B vapor-return gate, B tube in/out balls, A equivalents, any PRV block valves; stem turns, chain/lock status

test_plan.procedure: At Reboiler A (proxy) and B remnant: strap/UT shell ID, tape length, count/measure tubes; attempt controlled drain with level; sample to lab bomb for GC; review Feb 2012 nitrogen-charging and leak-through records.
test_plan.purpose: Close inventory + volume for trapped-liquid heating / vapor-pressure runs RB-ISO-01, RB-PRESS-01/02, RB-VOL-01.
test_plan.test: TP-05 Inventory and geometry - drain, sample and dimensional

test_plan.acceptance: Calibrated historian export: quench inlet 185-187 F confirmed +/-2 F, shell inlet ~130 F, flows timestamped to 08:33 opening and 08:36 rupture; gaps flagged

test_plan.procedure: At DCS historian + field FT (Fig.4 FT/FO), quench pumps: export 1-min (or faster) trends June 12-13, 2013; calibrate check RTDs/FTs in lab; note fouling-reduced flow through A vs jump on B opening.
test_plan.purpose: Provide initial/boundary conditions for heat-input transient without computing energy here.
test_plan.test: TP-09 Thermal-hydraulic historian retrieval + instrument check

assumptions: MAWP 300 psig / hydro 450 psig per task brief only - UNVERIFIED in p.6-13, see RFI-03; all pressure-vs-rating comparisons provisional pending nameplate/U-1 (TP-03).
B shell gates closed (blocked-in, no PRV path) at 08:33-08:36 per RFI-06; inferred from p.9 hazard + p.10 Fig.4 + rupture in ~3 min (p.11) despite PRV.
Shell contained liquid propane mixture (95% propane p.9) capable of hydraulic expansion, not N2 alone, per RFI-05; 3-min rupture implies incompressible/boiling inventory.
Initial shell ~54.44C (130F p.9) at bubble 18.75 bar; heating to 85-86.11C (185-187F p.9 + brief) per RFI-02/08.
Geometry ~18.5 ft x >5 ft shell, 3020x3/4-in 6-pass (p.9 fn11-13) APPROXIMATE per RFI-10; volumes not used for absolute sizing.
Cost classes are ASSUMPTION order-of-magnitude scoping only, Louisiana 2013-2016 basis, exclude business interruption (18-mo outage p.12).

findings.evidence: B offline 16 months (p.7); A quench flow dropped past day, meeting then supervisor troubleshooting (p.11); quench to B then ~3 min to rupture (p.11); quench ~185 degF (p.9), shell propane ~130 degF entering (p.9), ~95% propane balance propylene+C4s (p.9); fouling reduces flow/heat transfer (p.8). bubble_pressure quoted: 18.75 bar at 54.44C, 34.13 bar at 85.0C, 34.82 bar at 86.11C; blocked_in_pressure quoted: P1 18.75 bar 54.44 to 85.0C, bubble 34.13 bar at T2, beta 0.00812/K kappa 0.0006/bar, 13.5 bar/K, 432.0 bar / 6260 psig; fluid_properties quoted: 441.98 kg/m3 vapour 0.0 at 18.75 bar/54.44C to 337.44 kg/m3 vapour 0.0214 at 34.13 bar/85C; RB-HEAT-01 quoted: 5000 kg/h 11.3 m3/h vapour 0.0 to 130.48 m3/h vapour 1.0 at 20 bar, duty 471.88 kW.
findings.limiting_value: Hydraulic 6260 psig (blocked_in_pressure quoted) exceeds MAWP 300 psig and hydrotest 450 psig per task brief (UNVERIFIED in p.6-13); bubble 34.13 bar at 185 degF to 34.82 bar at 187 degF (bubble_pressure quoted, ASSUMPTION bara-to-psig ~480-490 psig) alone exceeds both ratings; 13.5 bar/K means ~0.1-0.2K exceeds MAWP from 18.75 bar. Explains 3-min delay, 30-ft missile/30000 lb/3.5-h fire/18-mo outage (p.11-p.12).
